claim_one_line: THE OBJECT'S ACTION EXISTS EXACTLY AT ITS MONODROMY, AND FAILS EXACTLY AT THE FORMAL SQUARE ROOT OF THE MONODROMY. An attempt at TOE row 4 (dynamics) rather than a report on it. THE THEOREM, which is this arc's own: a discrete Lagrangian L(a,b) generates through d2 L(a,b) + d1 L(b,c) = 0 a map that ALWAYS preserves omega = d1 d2 L da^db, hence det +1; an orientation-reversing map of a surface preserves NO area form; therefore AN ANTI-SYMPLECTIC MAP HAS NO DISCRETE LAGRANGIAN. Confirmed by exhaustive solve over the general quadratic ansatz, where the DEL relation always reads q(a+c) + 2(p+r)b = 0 -- a and c sharing a coefficient while the recursion needs them opposite. AND IT REACHES THE OBJECT (Q6e): T pulls the invariant Gelfand-Leray area form dx^dy/I_z back to MINUS itself on EVERY leaf, not only the one where the map linearises. B21 banked the anti-Poisson fact in the twenties and B448 banked the det -1; NEITHER DREW THE LAGRANGIAN CONSEQUENCE and nothing in the corpus does. THE JOIN, which is the result: B448 verified that T1 is the HALF-monodromy and the figure-eight monodromy is T1^2; this arc proves T1 has no action and T1^2 does. So the double tick was never a modelling choice -- T1 is not a thing the object does, it is a square root of the thing the object does, and it is precisely that square root which is anti-variational. The record now has THREE independent reasons the physical step is the double one, which no single arc had: ORIENTATION (L.P carries the swap, det -1, squaring restores it -- the paper's genesis), GEOMETRY (T1 is the half-monodromy, the monodromy is T1^2 = LoR -- B448), and VARIATIONAL (T1 is generated by no Lagrangian, T1^2 is -- here). Three faces of one det = -1.
